newsitem.title: GERMANY: G7 has no specific dollar targets - MOF's Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: G7 has no specific dollar targets - MOF's Sakakibara.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Japanese ministry of finance's International Finance Bureau, said on Saturday the G7 countries had no specific dollar target in mind.
"The group of seven nations has no specific dollar target", Sakakibara told reporters on the sidelines of the G7 meeting of finance ministers and central bank chiefs in Berlin.

But he said comments made earlier by German Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, in which Tietmeyer said the correction of the U.S. currency ought to end about now, suggested that some form of position might be adopted by the G7 countries on currencies.
"If the G7 are not going to make some sort of commitment on currencies such a remark may have not have been possible," he said, stressing again that this would not be in the form of a target.
The U.S. Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Canada and Britain are members of the G7.
Sakakibara is seen by the currency markets as one of the most influential Japanese officials.
